**Test image observations:**
- Tomato leaf with multiple small, dark brown to black spots scattered uniformly across the surface
- Spots are small (pinpoint to ~2-3mm), no obvious concentric rings
- General slight yellowing/chlorosis of the overall leaf tissue
- No visible webbing, no powdery coating, no velvety mold

**Candidate reasoning:**
- **Bacterial_Spot**: Small circular dark brown-to-black lesions, rarely >3mm, no prominent rings — matches well
- **Septoria_Leaf_Spot**: Small lesions with tan-gray centers and dark perimeter — possible, but centers appear uniformly dark in this image, not tan/gray
- **Target_Spot**: Starts as pinpoint dark spots, but typically develops concentric rings — not evident here

The Target_Spot reference shows similar small dark spots on green leaves, but the spots in the test image remain uniformly dark without the characteristic lighter centers or concentric rings. The scattered small dark spots with mild surrounding chlorosis best matches **Bacterial_Spot**, which features dark brown-to-black circular lesions rarely exceeding 3mm with possible faint yellow halos.
